title: Telemetry-driven benchmark suite and prefill/decode pacing experiments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Expand the benchmark harness to support telemetry-driven kernel routing experiments, fine-grained attention microbenchmarks, and prefill/decode pacing tests. Deliver stable golden baselines across model families, sequence-length distributions, and GPU classes and wire up CI perf gates that can detect regressions introduced by kernel changes, attention optimizations, or scheduler tuning.
context: Current benchmark suite covers macro workload mixes and kernel routing experiments but lacks per-request telemetry ingestion and workload slicing to validate prefill vs decode scheduling trade-offs. Recent kernel routing changes require a way to validate routing decisions under representative KV-cache/prefix patterns and attention op variants (relative vs rotary, fused MHA vs split kernels). We need reproducible baselines that map to customer-like traffic and CI checks that unblock fast iteration for runtime engineers.
tasks: Design telemetry schema for runtime traces: include model_id, kernel_variant, seq_prefill, seq_decode, kv_hit_ratio, batching_group, hw_target
Implement lightweight ingestion pipeline to export sampled request traces from staging runtime to bench harness
Add microbench modules for attention variants: measure fused vs unfused MHA, rotary vs relative position caching, and KV cache warm/cold prefill profiles
Create prefill/decode pacing runner to replay mixed prefill+decode patterns with configurable pacing (ms inter-request) and background batching pressure
Generate golden baselines: run suite across small, medium, large models and A100, H100, and T4 targets; store artifacts and summarized metrics
Define CI perf gate thresholds and implement auto-bisect metadata collection for failing gates
Integrate dashboard reporting and alerting for baseline drift and flaky tests
Write docs and runbook for adding new kernel variants and updating golden baselines
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness can consume sampled telemetry traces and synthesize replay scenarios that reproduce observed prefill/decode mixes
Microbench results for attention variants produce <5% noise for median latency over 100 runs on stable hardware
Golden baselines produced and uploaded for at least 3 model classes and 3 GPU classes
CI perf gates reject regressions larger than configured thresholds (default: +5% median latency or +10% p95) and save artifacts required for triage
On-call and runtime teams can add new kernel variants through a documented flow without changing CI plumbing
risks: Telemetry volume: full trace retention is expensive; need sampling heuristics to keep cost acceptable
Hardware availability: running exhaustive matrix across model sizes and GPUs may be constrained by lab resources
Flaky tests: network and scheduler nondeterminism can cause noisy results if not isolated
False positives in CI gates if baselines are not sufficiently representative of production workloads
